mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE values.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) crosses above 0.25%, it indicates monetary tightening, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following FEDFUNDS crossing above 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in both real estate investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following simultaneous increases in RSAFS and HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) during an expansionary regime suggests increased economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following INDPRO increases during expansion.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a strong economy, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following positive GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following significant PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates an accommodative monetary policy and strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during a late-cycle expansion indicates continued demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 5-day windows following HOUST increases during late-cycle expansion.
